schools.name: Holywell Bay School of Surf
schools.base: On the beachfront at Holywell Bay, at the surf life saving club
schools.note: Small-group, private, family and group-private lessons of about two hours, starting with a safety briefing on the sand. You need to be a confident swimmer; wetsuit and beginner foam board are included.

schools.name: Cornwall Surfing Academy
schools.base: Holywell Bay Holiday Park (TR8 5PR); arrive 30 minutes early for wetsuit fitting
schools.note: A family-friendly school teaching at Holywell Bay and Fistral, including two-hour private lessons on Holywell beach. Students need to be able to swim 50 metres in open water.

lessonsIntro: Holywell Bay is a big, sandy National Trust beach between Crantock and Perranporth, with a surf school based right on the beachfront. Visit Cornwall notes lessons run throughout the year.

text: Holywell is exposed to large Atlantic swells, and Visit Cornwall says the surf is at its best at low and mid tide. The two ends behave differently: the north end takes the full force of the swell and gets much bigger, while the south end is more sheltered from south-westerly winds by the rock islands offshore. On bigger days, learners should stick to the gentler water with a school rather than heading out alone.

RNLI lifeguards patrol daily from 16 May to 27 September 2026, 10am to 6pm, and the RNLI has reported rescuing people from rip currents here. Swim and bodyboard between the red and yellow flags. Holywell Bay School of Surf says you need to be a confident swimmer for lessons, and Cornwall Surfing Academy asks that you can swim 50 metres in open water. St Cuthbert's Cave can only be reached at low tide.

cards.label: Level
cards.title: Beginners with a school
cards.text: Lessons run all year, but the beach takes big Atlantic swell, so learn with an instructor.

cards.label: Best time
cards.title: Low to mid tide
cards.text: Visit Cornwall says Holywell is at its best around low and mid tide; lifeguards are on from mid-May to late September.

cards.label: Watch out for
cards.title: Big swell and rips
cards.text: The north end gets much bigger waves, and the RNLI has reported rip current rescues here.

hireIntro: We couldn't confirm a standalone surf hire shop at Holywell Bay. Both local schools include a wetsuit and board in their lessons.

text: Lessons here come with a wetsuit and a beginner foam board, so you don't need your own kit to start. If you're bringing your own, a soft-top or mini mal suits the beach's mid-tide waves for learners. Sea temperatures at Holywell range from about 9-10C in early March to 15-18C in mid August, so a full wetsuit is needed all year.

cards.label: Board
cards.title: Foam board included in lessons
cards.text: Both schools supply beginner foam boards; improvers can step up to a mini mal.

cards.label: Wetsuit
cards.title: 4/3 in summer, 5mm in winter
cards.text: A 4/3mm or 3/2mm with boots in summer; a 5/4mm or 5/3mm with gloves, boots and a hood in late winter.

cards.label: Other craft
cards.title: Bodyboards between the flags
cards.text: Holywell is popular with bodyboarders; stay between the red and yellow flags when lifeguards are on.

shopsIntro: We didn't find a surf shop at Holywell Bay, so for kit you'll need to head to Newquay or Perranporth.
shopsText: Holywell is a small village with a National Trust car park next to the beach, and none of the sources we checked list a surf shop here. Newquay has several, including Ann's Cottage at Fistral and Sunset Surf and Slide and Glide on Fore Street, while Perranporth has Bathsheba Surf on St Pirans Road.

lessons.q: Which surf schools teach at Holywell Bay?
lessons.a: Holywell Bay School of Surf, based on the beachfront at the surf life saving club, and Cornwall Surfing Academy, based at Holywell Bay Holiday Park.

lessons.q: Do I need to be able to swim for a lesson at Holywell?
lessons.a: Yes. Holywell Bay School of Surf asks that you're a confident swimmer, and Cornwall Surfing Academy asks that you can swim 50 metres unaided in open water.

lessons.q: What's the best tide for surfing Holywell Bay?
lessons.a: Visit Cornwall says the surf is at its best around low and mid tide.

hire.q: Can I hire a surfboard at Holywell Bay?
hire.a: We couldn't confirm a standalone hire shop. Both local schools include a wetsuit and foam board with lessons, so booking a lesson is the easiest way to get kit.

hire.q: What wetsuit do I need at Holywell?
hire.a: In summer a 3/2mm or 4/3mm with boots; from late autumn to spring, a 5mm suit with gloves, boots and a hood.

shops.q: Is there a surf shop in Holywell Bay?
shops.a: Not that we could find. The nearest surf shops are in Newquay and Perranporth.

National Trust car park near the beach; stream and dunes

gaps: No standalone board/wetsuit hire and no surf shop could be confirmed at Holywell Bay (both lists empty). Holywell Bay School of Surf's own site doesn't state a minimum age (Cornish Secrets says family classes from age 7, not used in the note). Trevornick holiday park partners with Holywell Bay School of Surf for guest lessons, but it's not clear non-guests can book through Trevornick, so it's not listed separately. Search budget ran out before I could look for seasonal beach hire kiosks at Holywell.
